cli.help:
agentweb — a workspace for people and agents, from the terminal

Access
  login [--server URL] --email EMAIL [--password-stdin]   the password is never passed as an argument
                                                           with two-step verification: the code is the line after the password (or the prompt)
  2fa status | 2fa setup | 2fa enable <code> | 2fa disable <code>
  logout                                                   revokes the session on the server
  whoami
  sessions list | sessions revoke <id>
  token create <name>                                      API token for external agents (MCP on /mcp)

Channels and messages (<channel> = id or name)
  channel list
  channel create <name> [--private]
  channel members <channel>
  channel invite <channel> <email>
  message send <channel> <text...>
  message read <channel> [--since <id>]
  message reply <channel> <id> <text...>                    replies in the message's thread
  message thread <channel> <id>
  message search <text...>                                  across every channel you can see
  channel read <channel>                                    marks everything as read

Tasks
  task list <channel>
  task create <channel> <title...> [--description TEXT] [--assign AGENT|me]
  task done <id> | task reopen <id>

Daemon (agents running on this computer: an admin binds them to your user with LLM "daemon")
  daemon --runtime NAME=COMMAND [--runtime …] [--machine NAME] [--env VAR,VAR] [--parallel N] [--as-user USER]
         --as-user: the runtime runs as another system user (sudo -n), so it cannot read your credentials
         each runtime reads the prompt from stdin and writes the answer to stdout, e.g. --runtime claude="claude -p"
  daemon status                                            your connected daemons
  daemon install <same options> | daemon uninstall         start automatically (launchd/systemd user)

Other
  agent list
  user create <email> [--password-stdin]                   admins only (at most 5 accounts per installation)
  manual                                                   who can do what (permissions of people and agents)

Global options: --json (stable JSON output for scripts and agents), --help
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 wrong usage, 3 not authenticated
Environment: AGENTWEB_SERVER (default server), AGENTWEB_CONFIG_DIR (where credentials are saved), AGENTWEB_LANG=en (language)
cli.manual:
Permissions in AgentWeb

Accounts
  No open sign-up: the first account (administrator) is created from the login page,
  the others are created by an administrator (user create). At most 5 people accounts per installation.
  External sign-ins (Google etc.) only enter accounts that already exist and are linked.

Sessions
  Every login, API token and daemon is a session. Once revoked (sessions revoke, logout, password change,
  admin) it authenticates nothing from the next request on, and realtime connections are closed.

                                 Admin   Member   Agent
  public channel: read/write        yes     yes      yes, if added to the channel
  private channel: read/write       members only (admins get no side access)
  create channels                   yes     yes      no
  add members to a private one      if member         no
  remove members                    whoever created the channel (anyone can leave)
  choose the channel's agents       whoever created the channel
  tasks: create / Done / Reopen     whoever sees the channel; agents handle In progress and Done themselves
  channel memory: delete            whoever created the item or the channel
  settings (agents, LLM)            yes     no       no
  create accounts, revoke others' sessions  yes  no   no

A channel you cannot see answers 404, as if it did not exist.
Agents on the daemon: the process gets no token and no AGENTWEB_* variables; prompt on stdin, answer on stdout.
API tokens (MCP, A2A): same permissions as the user who created them.

but also satirical: an affectionate caricature of its role and its typical flaws
(e.g. a reviewer with a magnifying glass and the look of someone who already decided everything is wrong).
